title: Testing register in Postman
idea: Testing register in Postman means sending a valid body, a repeat and a broken body, then checking the status and body of each reply.
points: Send `POST {{baseUrl}}/api/v1/auth/register` with Body raw JSON, as set up earlier.
A valid body returns `201`; the user in `data` has no password field.
Send the same body again: the duplicate check should answer `409`.
Check the mailbox your `MAIL_*` settings point to; the reply cannot prove delivery.

code.title: Postman test script
code.caption: Postman runs this after each response and shows pass or fail. It cannot run here, so it is not recorded.

walk.text: A script belongs to one request. Postman runs it after the response arrives.
`pm.test` names a check. `pm.response.to.have.status` asserts the status.
`pm.response.json()` parses the body; `pm.expect` checks fields, including that `password` is absent.
The repeat is a second request with its own script: expect `409` and `success: false`.

pitfalls: Send the first request twice and the second gets `409`: change the username and email.
Keep real passwords out of saved requests; collections get shared and exported.

quiz.q: You send the same valid register body twice. What does the second reply return?
quiz.why: The duplicate check finds the saved user and throws `ApiError` with 409. Nothing is saved or emailed.

takeaway: Send the failures too: each status is a choice your code made.
